title: Sesame bagels
summary: Chewy, ring-shaped rolls from a psyllium almond dough, briefly boiled and baked with a sesame crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment. Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer.
Whisk the almond flour, psyllium, baking powder and salt. Add the egg whites and lemon juice, then the boiling water, and mix quickly into a dough. Rest 10 minutes.
With wet hands, divide into 6 and roll each into a ball. Push a finger through the middle and widen the hole to about 3 cm (1¼ in); it closes up in the oven.
Lower the bagels into the simmering water two at a time for 30 seconds, then lift out with a slotted spoon onto the sheet.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle generously with sesame seeds.
Bake 45–50 minutes, until well browned and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack before slicing.
tips: Psyllium gives this dough a bread-like chew; brands differ, and some darken the crumb purple-grey — it is harmless.
The short simmer sets the surface and helps a shiny crust; skip it if the dough feels too soft to handle.

origin.history: The bagel is a Polish-Jewish bread. Records from Kraków in the early 1600s are often cited as the first written mention of bajgiel. Jewish immigrants carried the boiled-then-baked ring to North America around 1900, where it became a New York staple.
